title: Unauthenticated JSON bodies are still decoded before principal(); one 8 MiB request costs about 200 MB of transient memory and 0.4-0.7 s of event-loop time before the 401
description: The F1 fix (PR #16) caps request bodies before routing, at 8 MiB (AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY) for JSON routes. That cap is identical for unauthenticated and authenticated clients. FastAPI's get_request_handler (fastapi 0.161.1) reads the body and decodes the JSON before solve_dependencies runs principal()/human_only. On the async route (call_tool, api.py:274) the decode runs on the event loop. A body of empty objects decodes at about 26x its size. Parent-live check on a real uvicorn server (127.0.0.1, stub Docker client, 1 GiB container, dummy human token, no Authorization header, 8,388,580-byte body to POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/exec): idle RSS 59 MB. One request returned 401 after 0.69 s, with RSS 260 MB afterwards and a high-water mark of 268 MB. Four concurrent requests reached a 703 MB high-water mark, and a human GET /healthz sent during that burst took 1.23 s against 0.003 s idle. Eight concurrent requests reached 734 MB, with every request answered 401 in under 4 s and healthz at 0.47 s. The server stayed alive and was not OOM-killed in any run. So the amplification and the missing authentication ordering are reproduced, but the effect is bounded in the tested configuration: transient memory, concurrent decodes appear to be serialised by the single event loop (peak flattened from 4 to 8 clients), and impact was a sub-second to about 1 s stall. Nothing in the repository limits the effect further. cli.py:127 passes no limit_concurrency, deploy/docker-compose.yml sets no memory limit, and the bundled Caddyfile allows 256MB per request by default. Whether this causes an OOM-kill or a sustained stall of the shared control plane (human approval UI, audit chain) depends on the deployed memory limit, the supervisor restart behavior, and the attacker's sustained bandwidth, none of which the repository fixes. Attacker cost is one 8 MiB upload per 0.4-0.7 s of event-loop time, so about 12-20 MB/s of sustained upload would keep the loop busy. The run-4 finding (unbounded body size, multipart spooling) is fixed: bytes are now capped and the upload form is parsed only after screen_human. What remains is bounded per-request work that is not tied to authentication.
claimed_root_cause: Authentication dependencies run after FastAPI's body-reading and JSON-decoding stage. The only pre-auth bound is a byte cap (8 MiB) sized for the largest authenticated payload (an escaped 1 MiB write_file). It does not account for the roughly 26x object-graph amplification of JSON, there is no smaller cap or credential check for requests that carry no Authorization header, and no concurrency limit on pre-auth decodes (no uvicorn limit_concurrency, no container memory limit, no proxy JSON-route cap below 256MB).

trace.scope: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool} (async call_tool, body: ToolCall, Depends(principal)); same shape at create_sandbox api.py:233, restore api.py:264, decide api.py:309
trace.description: A client with no token sends a JSON body of up to 8 MiB to a route it knows answers 401.
Content-Length is checked against the cap only (8 MiB for non-upload routes, cap from config.py:65). The check is independent of whether credentials are present.
Streamed bytes are counted up to the cap and handed to the app. Bodies at or under 8 MiB pass unchanged.
Runs only after FastAPI has buffered the body and json.loads has built the full object graph (about 26x the body for empty objects). It then raises 401 at the missing Authorization header.

evidence.description: _BodyLimit is installed with json_max=settings.max_body_bytes and applies to every non-upload route regardless of authentication. api.py:171 _NoFraming only adds response headers.
max_body_bytes defaults to 8 MiB, sized so an escaped 1 MiB write_file fits. This is a pre-auth ceiling of 8 MiB per request.
uvicorn.run passes no limit_concurrency, so concurrent pre-auth decodes are not bounded in source.
request_body max_size defaults to 256MB (AGENTBOX_PROXY_MAX_BODY) for every route, so the shipped proxy does not enforce the 8 MiB cap or anything smaller on JSON routes.
The agentbox service has no mem_limit or deploy.resources limits. The same process serves the approval UI and the audit chain.

Parent-live result (real uvicorn, 1 GiB container, no auth): 8,388,580-byte body gives 401 in 0.69 s, RSS 59 to 260 MB (hwm 268). 4 concurrent give hwm 703 MB and healthz 1.23 s. 8 concurrent give hwm 734 MB and healthz 0.47 s. No OOM at 1 GiB.
Hunter-local check: tracemalloc peak 27.4 MB for a 1.05 MB body and 54.9 MB for 2.10 MB, both 401, confirming the linear ~26x amplification before the dependency runs.

blockers: Deployed memory limit of the agentbox control-plane container or host is outside the repository. The compose file sets none, and the parent-live 1 GiB test survived 8 concurrent 8 MiB requests with a 734 MB high-water mark, so an OOM-kill is not shown. A smaller limit (for example 512 MiB) or more concurrent connections might trigger one.

Sustained-load behavior (event-loop starvation of the human UI and approvals under repeated pre-auth requests) and the supervisor restart policy were not measured, because the audit rules forbid stress or saturation testing. The measured stall was about 1.2 s for a 4-request burst.
The deployed edge may enforce a stricter body cap, connection or rate limit than the bundled Caddyfile (default 256MB, no rate limit). That is the owner's configuration.

validation_plan.local: Repeat the parent-live harness (agents/parent-live/parent_live_preauth_json.py) in a disposable container with --network none and a tighter limit such as --memory 512m, with 8 MiB bodies at 2, 4 and 8 concurrent, and record the exit status (OOM-kill or not), hwm and healthz latency. Stop at the first OOM-kill. Fix check: after adding a smaller pre-auth cap, or a pre-body Authorization-present gate in _BodyLimit, the same unauthenticated requests should return 413 or 401 with no measurable RSS growth.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks the memory limit and restart policy of the agentbox control-plane container or host. Owner checks whether the TLS proxy or edge applies a per-route or JSON body cap below 8 MiB (the bundled Caddyfile allows 256MB on every route) and any per-client rate or connection limit. Owner confirms that a stall of 1 s or more on the single uvicorn process, which also serves the human approval queue and the audit chain, is acceptable. Suggested hardening: reject JSON-route requests without an Authorization header or session cookie before reading the body (a pre-body gate in _BodyLimit), set a lower AGENTBOX_PROXY_MAX_BODY for non-upload routes, add limit_concurrency, and set a container mem_limit.

title: Desktop WebSocket handler blocks the shared event loop on SQLite and audit locks, so one desktop connect stalls every HTTP route
description: The async route /sandboxes/{sid}/desktop/ws (api.py:408-418) and desktop_ws.relay make synchronous SQLite, threading.Lock and Docker SDK calls directly on the asyncio event loop. These are the session lookup, vnc_command (_rec plus containers.get), the log_human audit write, add_conn, the per-message touch() in control mode, the 30 s session re-check and the log_best_effort audit write on disconnect. While another SQLite connection holds the write lock (for example retention.prune's BEGIN IMMEDIATE, run by the host operator) or a worker holds AuditLog._lock, one authenticated desktop WS connect or disconnect freezes the whole control plane for up to the 5 s default sqlite busy timeout or the remaining lock hold. That covers every HTTP route, including human approvals and deletes, agent tool responses and /healthz. A desktop-link session scoped to one sandbox, or a desktop page that auto-reconnects, can repeat the stall while the condition lasts. An unauthenticated upgrade with a junk cookie stalls the loop only in a narrower case: a human desktop write (login, ticket, takeover or handback) is itself waiting on the SQLite write lock while holding DesktopControl._lock, and the loop then waits on that lock in session_scope. This undoes the design intent at api.py:158-160, which keeps blocking tool work off the human API's executor. The attacker cannot create the long lock hold, only trigger the WS event while one exists.
root_cause: desktop_ws (api.py:409-418) and relay (desktop_ws.py:20-21,41,57,72,91) call blocking functions without run_in_threadpool. The calls are DesktopControl.session_scope (desktop.py:152-160), AgentBox.log_human and log_best_effort, which reach AuditLog.append (BEGIN IMMEDIATE under AuditLog._lock, default 5 s busy timeout; audit.py:293-294), SandboxManager._rec and containers.get (sandbox.py:185-186,230), and DesktopControl.touch and add_conn. DesktopControl also holds its in-memory threading.Lock across SQLite writes (desktop.py:135-139, plus issue_ticket, redeem, take and release), so the event loop inherits any SQLite write wait that a worker thread is in.
intended_behavior: The event loop never waits on SQLite, on threading locks held across I/O, or on the Docker daemon. A slow or locked database, or a slow audit read, should delay only the request that needs it and never unrelated HTTP and WebSocket traffic for other sandboxes.

trace.description: Async WebSocket route; the session cookie comes from the upgrade request, so any desktop-link holder (or any cookie value, for the narrow unauthenticated case) reaches it.
box.desktop.session(cookie, sid) is called synchronously on the event loop.
Takes the threading.Lock _lock, which worker threads hold across SQLite writes (new_session at desktop.py:135-139, take, release). It blocks the loop thread while it waits.
vnc_command runs on the loop: _rec takes SandboxManager._lock plus a SQLite read (sandbox.py:185-186), then containers.get makes a blocking Docker HTTP call (sandbox.py:230).
box.log_human (service.py:658-662) runs on the loop and calls AuditLog.append.
Under AuditLog._lock, BEGIN IMMEDIATE waits up to the default 5 s sqlite busy timeout for the write lock. The whole event loop is blocked for the wait, then the connect fails with close code 1011.

evidence.description: The disconnect audit write (log_best_effort) also runs inline on the loop in finally, so closing a tab can stall the loop too.
touch() takes DesktopControl._lock on the loop for every client message in control mode.
The 30 s session re-check calls box.desktop.session synchronously on the loop, while the handback just below it correctly uses run_in_threadpool.
prune holds the SQLite write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, connection timeout 30) for its whole delete transaction. It is a host CLI operation.

verify() reads the whole audit table under AuditLog._lock. recent() (audit.py:321-326) does an unindexed COUNT(*) under the same lock. Both are human-triggered reads whose duration grows with the agent-grown audit table.
The comment at api.py:158-160 states the design intent: keep blocking tool work off the shared executor so the agent cannot freeze the human API.
new_session holds _lock across DELETE and INSERT, so it can wait out the busy timeout while holding the lock the loop needs.

conditions.description: For the 5 s audit-write stall: a valid desktop-link session (scope one sandbox) or a full UI session. For the DesktopControl._lock stall: no valid session is needed (any cookie value reaches session_scope), but see the timing condition.

A concurrent long holder must exist: retention.prune's BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same DB (operator maintenance), a worker inside AuditLog._lock (verify or recent over a large table), or a human desktop write that is waiting on the SQLite write lock while holding DesktopControl._lock. The requester cannot create the hold itself.

The stall is bounded by the 5 s default sqlite busy timeout for each write attempt, or by the remaining audit-lock hold, which grows with the number of audit rows (measured 0.77-0.84 s for verify() over 100k rows). Docker daemon latency in containers.get was not measured.

execution.attacker_perspective: A holder of a desktop link (scoped human session), or just an open desktop tab that auto-reconnects 1.5 s after a server close, connects to the desktop WebSocket while another SQLite connection holds the write lock or a worker holds the audit lock.
payloads: /home/user/agentbox/docs/security-audit/run-5/tools/sbx v-ws /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h.py (the hunter's h-ws harness copied unchanged: real agentbox.api.build() app, docker.from_env replaced by an in-process fake, dummy human token hum_ddd..., sandbox sb_x template desktop, desktop-link session from box.desktop.new_session('sb_x'))
instructions: Ran in the approved sandbox (no network, no Docker, uid 65534) with AGENTBOX_HOME=/scratch/home, AGENTBOX_DOCKER_CLI=/bin/false and AGENTBOX_MIN_FREE=0 against the audited tree at 346df29.

In each scenario a holder thread keeps a contention in place: a second sqlite3 connection in BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 7 s, a worker inside AuditLog._lock for 4 s, or BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a worker calling box.desktop.new_session().
Open TestClient.websocket_connect('/sandboxes/sb_x/desktop/ws?mode=view') with the link-session cookie, a junk cookie or no cookie, then 0.3 s later time GET /healthz on the same app.
execution.observed_result: Reproduced independently. Baseline healthz 0.0 s. Link-session WS under the SQLite write lock: healthz 4.71 s and WS closed 1011 after 5.02 s. Junk or no cookie under the same write lock: 0.0 s. Junk cookie while new_session waited on the write lock (holding DesktopControl._lock): healthz 4.41 s. Link-session WS while AuditLog._lock was held 4 s: healthz 3.51 s. Junk cookie under the audit lock: 0.0 s. audit.verify() over 100k rows in a loop: healthz 0.2 s (a short stall).

remediation.strategy: Move every blocking call in desktop_ws and relay off the event loop with run_in_threadpool, or the dedicated pool for audit writes. Stop holding DesktopControl._lock across SQLite I/O by guarding the DB with a separate lock, so touch(), lease() and add_conn() never wait on a database. Add a regression test: while a second connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or a thread holds AuditLog._lock, a desktop WS connect must leave GET /healthz latency under 0.5 s.

code_changes.fixed_code:
@app.websocket("/sandboxes/{sid}/desktop/ws")
    async def desktop_ws(ws: WebSocket, sid: str, mode: str = "view"):
        cookie = ws.cookies.get(D.COOKIE)
        session = await run_in_threadpool(box.desktop.session, cookie, sid)
        if not session or not same_origin(ws.headers) or mode not in ("view", "control"):
            await ws.close(code=4401)
            return
        if not await run_in_threadpool(box.desktop.may_connect, sid, session, mode):
            await ws.close(code=4403)
            return
        await relay(ws, box, sid, session, mode, cookie)

try:
        argv = await run_in_threadpool(box.sandboxes.vnc_command, sid, mode == "view")
        await run_in_threadpool(box.log_human, "desktop_connect", sid, {"session": session, "mode": mode})
    except (SandboxError, ServiceError):
        await ws.close(code=1011)
        return
    # also: await run_in_threadpool for box.desktop.add_conn / touch / session in session_watch,
    # and run the log_best_effort call in finally on a worker thread instead of inline

# keep self._lock for the in-memory dicts only; guard self._db with a separate self._db_lock,
# and never take self._db_lock while holding self._lock, so touch()/lease()/add_conn() never wait on SQLite

likelihood.reason: Needs a long SQLite or audit lock holder to coincide with a desktop WS event. The holders are the operator's prune, a human audit view over a large table, or a human desktop write blocked behind such a hold. A desktop-link holder or an auto-reconnecting tab can repeat the trigger but cannot create the hold.

impact.reason: Temporary freeze of all control-plane HTTP and WS traffic, observed at 3.5-4.7 s per event and repeatable while the condition lasts. No data or authority gain, and no persistent denial.

confidence.reason: The event-loop stall was reproduced independently with the real handler, audit and SQLite code (healthz 4.71 s, 4.41 s and 3.51 s, matching the hunter's figures). Real prune durations and Docker daemon latency in containers.get were not measured, because Docker is faked offline.

title: Interrupted prune deletes the only archive of audit rows it has already committed as pruned
description: retention.prune writes the archive, then deletes the audit and approval rows and records an audit_anchor holding the archive's sha256, all in one transaction. The inner handler issues ROLLBACK on any exception, and the outer handler unlinks the archive on any BaseException. Neither handler checks whether COMMIT already succeeded. If a KeyboardInterrupt surfaces right after COMMIT returns (Ctrl-C during the fsync-bound COMMIT), the inner ROLLBACK raises OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active'). The outer handler then deletes the archive. The database says rows 1..N were pruned into an archive with a recorded sha256, and that archive no longer exists. verify() still reports ok with 'pruned through #N'. verify_archives can no longer pass, and a re-run finds nothing to prune. The pruned audit history and its tamper evidence are lost, which contradicts the invariant that a failed prune leaves the database and archive consistent.
root_cause: The archive cleanup at retention.py:130-131 runs on any exception rather than only when the prune transaction did not commit. The inner handler (retention.py:127-129) runs ROLLBACK unconditionally, even when the transaction has already committed at retention.py:126. Any exception that surfaces after COMMIT therefore both masks itself with a ROLLBACK error and triggers the unlink of the archive that the durable anchor row refers to.
intended_behavior: The archive is removed only if the prune transaction did not commit. Once the anchor row referencing the archive's sha256 is durable, the archive must be kept whatever exception follows. The failure should be reported as 'pruned; archive kept at <path>'. ROLLBACK should be issued only while a transaction is active.

trace.description: Host operator runs `agentbox prune --before ... --archive ...`. It calls retention.prune on Settings().db_path and catches only ValueError, FileExistsError and RuntimeError (cli.py:322-324).
The archive is written, fsynced and hashed before the transaction starts.
Inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, audit rows are deleted and an audit_anchor row with the archive name and sha256 is inserted.
COMMIT makes the deletion and anchor durable. A SIGINT arriving during this call is raised as KeyboardInterrupt right after it returns, still inside the inner try.
Unconditional ROLLBACK raises OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active'), chained on the KeyboardInterrupt.
archive.unlink deletes the only copy of the rows the committed anchor says were archived.

evidence.description: The archive is unlinked on any BaseException with no check of commit state.
ROLLBACK is issued without checking conn.in_transaction, so it raises after a successful COMMIT.
verify() starts at the latest anchor, so it keeps passing after the archive is lost and hides the loss.

verify_archives reads the archive and compares its sha256 to the anchor. With the archive deleted it raises FileNotFoundError, and with an empty archive list it fails on the anchor/archive count mismatch (audit.py:353-354).
cmd_prune catches only ValueError, FileExistsError and RuntimeError. The OperationalError surfaces as a traceback.

conditions.description: Host operator running the prune CLI with direct DB file access. No remote or agent principal is involved.

SIGINT (Ctrl-C or a supervisor sending SIGINT) must arrive while COMMIT executes or in the few bytecodes after it inside the inner try. COMMIT of a large prune is fsync-bound, so the window is real for the large prunes the command is meant for.
At least one audit or terminal approval row is older than the cutoff, so prune reaches the transaction.

execution.attacker_perspective: No adversary is needed. This is an operator interrupt of a command whose interrupted-prune handling is supposed to be safe. The effect is permanent loss of the archived audit rows and their tamper evidence for the pruned range.
payloads: v-prune p.py: AuditLog fixture with 5 rows before the cutoff and 2 after. retention.sqlite3 is shimmed with a Connection subclass whose execute('COMMIT') performs the real COMMIT and then calls signal.raise_signal(SIGINT). Then prune(db, cut, archive) is called and verify() and verify_archives([archive]) are run.
instructions: Run tools/sbx v-prune /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/p.py (no network, read-only /target, uid 65534).
Read the exception, whether the archive exists, the audit/anchor rows, and the verify() and verify_archives() results.

The hunter's artifacts agents/h-retention/artifacts/h.out and h2.out show the same with the full harness. h2 uses a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real 20k-row COMMIT and hit the inner except in 5 of 5 attempts.
execution.observed_result: Independent run: prune raised OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active') with __context__ KeyboardInterrupt. The archive no longer exists. The audit table holds 3 rows starting at id 6, with anchor (seq 1, last_id 5, 'x.jsonl.gz'). verify() returned ok=True, pruned_through=5. verify_archives([archive]) raised FileNotFoundError. Hunter's h2.out confirms a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real COMMIT reaches the inner except with the 20000 rows committed.

remediation.strategy: Make archive cleanup depend on commit state, not on whether an exception was raised. Roll back only while conn.in_transaction is true. In the outer handler, check whether an audit_anchor row with this archive's name and sha256 exists, and unlink only if it does not. If the check itself fails, keep the archive. Report a post-commit interruption as 'pruned; archive kept at <path>' rather than a raw OperationalError. Optionally fsync the archive's parent directory after creating it. Add a regression test where a Connection factory raises KeyboardInterrupt after a successful COMMIT, and assert the archive remains and verify_archives([archive]) passes.

likelihood.reason: Needs a SIGINT to land during or just after COMMIT of a host-only CLI command run by the operator. The window is short but real for large, fsync-bound prunes, and Ctrl-C on a slow-looking command is a common operator action.

impact.reason: The only remaining copy of the pruned audit rows and finished approvals is permanently destroyed, while the in-DB anchor and verify() report the history as cleanly archived. Full-history verification becomes impossible from then on. There is no confidentiality impact and no remote attacker.

confidence.reason: The source lines match. I reproduced the outcome independently in the sandbox with a COMMIT-then-SIGINT shim. The hunter's real-timing harness produced the same behaviour in 5 of 5 attempts. The synthetic shim models the timing: a signal delivered during COMMIT is raised as KeyboardInterrupt on return from the C call.

title: GUI burst opened during a human takeover lets the control plane kill the human's processes and charge human edits to the agent
description: AgentBox._snapshot closes and opens an agent GUI burst without taking gui_lock and without checking the takeover lease. If an approved GUI click/type/key is decided while a lease is held, or if an agent click/type/key whose pre-input docker commit overlaps POST /desktop/takeover, a new burst is installed with a baseline taken mid-takeover. _run_tool then raises HumanControl (call_tool returns 423, decide marks the approval failed) but nothing discards the burst. When close_idle runs, or the next agent burst closes it after handback, _stop_strays SIGKILLs as the desktop user every uid-1001 process the human started after that baseline in a session absent from it (terminal shells and jobs started from them). _finish also records the human's /workspace edits as agent gui_changes under the agent burst's snapshot_id. Takeover closes the burst at service.py:582 precisely so that human activity stays out of agent bursts, and this path bypasses that. The agent can choose when the kill happens, because any agent tool call or GET /approvals/{aid} runs close_idle. Path (a) is demonstrated against the real Docker engine and desktop image. Path (b) rests on source plus a local deterministic schedule: the race window is the docker commit duration, which was not timed live, and the agent cannot force a takeover into it. Impact is bounded: lost human background work (windowed apps are kept) and misattributed audit rows, not agent escalation.
root_cause: Burst open/close in _snapshot (service.py:261-276) is not serialized with takeover (gui_lock) and is not conditioned on the lease. GuiBursts.needs_snapshot (gui_bursts.py:61) checks the lease only before a multi-second commit, and decide (service.py:467) does not check it at all. The HumanControl handlers in call_tool (service.py:373-381) and decide (service.py:477-480) leave the burst that _snapshot just opened in _gui_burst. A baseline taken during the lease is later used for stray kill and change attribution.
intended_behavior: No agent GUI burst (baseline, later stray kill, gui_changes attribution) exists while a human takeover lease is held. Takeover closes the agent burst under gui_lock (service.py:582) so that human processes and edits are never judged against an agent baseline, and every later burst open is serialized against the lease.

trace.description: The agent token calls click/type/key (api.py:278 calls box.call_tool with actor=agent). A pending GUI approval is decided via POST /approvals/{aid} (api.py:308) or POST /ui/approvals/{aid}/{decision} (web.py:242), both reaching AgentBox.decide.
The lease and takeover_pending check happens only here, before the docker commit. With no lease yet it returns True and the commit starts.
The allow path calls _snapshot without gui_lock. decide calls _snapshot at service.py:467 with no lease check at all.
Takeover takes gui_lock, which is free because _snapshot does not hold it. It closes the burst (none open yet) and installs the lease at service.py:584.
After the commit returns, bursts.open records a baseline of desktop-user pids and a /workspace manifest taken while the lease is held (gui_bursts.py:73-87).

_check_control raises HumanControl. call_tool returns 423 (service.py:373-381) and decide marks the approval failed (service.py:477-480). The burst stays in _gui_burst and no input time is marked (mark_input is never reached), so it already counts as idle.

Run from any call_tool (service.py:285) or expire_stale (service.py:424, reached by GET /approvals/{aid}, api.py:288-290). It submits close() of the mid-lease burst while the lease is still held. Alternatively _snapshot's close('next_burst') (service.py:263) closes it after handback.
Human-started desktop-user processes in sessions absent from the mid-lease baseline are classified as strays (line 78). Windowed ones go to kept.
kill -KILL of the human's processes as the desktop user (via GuiBursts._stop_strays, gui_bursts.py:95). _finish (gui_bursts.py:147) logs the human's /workspace edits as agent gui_changes.

evidence.description: _snapshot closes (263) and opens (268) the burst with no gui_lock and no lease or takeover_pending check.
decide calls _snapshot unconditionally for an approved GUI input, even while desktop.lease(sid) is set.
The HumanControl handler returns 423 without discarding the burst opened by _snapshot. decide (477-480) likewise only marks the approval failed.
takeover closes the burst so that human changes stay out of agent bursts. The open in _snapshot can happen after this close, so the intent is bypassed.
_stop_strays computes gui_strays against the burst baseline and kills them.
close_idle treats a burst with no recorded input time as idle (_gui_input_at.get(sid, 0.0)). A burst opened by a blocked input therefore closes on the next close_idle even though the lease is held.
Docstring of gui_strays: processes in sessions absent at burst start (terminal shells, nohup/setsid jobs) are stopped.
GET /approvals/{aid} is callable by the agent token and runs expire_stale -> close_idle, so the agent chooses when the close happens.

Live run against the real Docker engine and agentbox-desktop:0.1: with click gated by policy, takeover, agent click returned 202, human approve returned status failed (HumanControl) with burst_open true. A desktop-user setsid job (pid 400) started during the lease was then SIGKILLed at close_idle with the lease still held. Audit shows human_takeover, snapshot(click), tool_error, then gui_processes_stopped reason idle for 'sleep 600'. (The artifact's burst_baseline_size 0 is a script key mismatch, 'procs' versus the burst's 'pids', and does not affect the kill.)

conditions.description: Agent token for its own desktop sandbox (lowest-trust network principal). Path (a) also needs the human to take over and decide the approval.

Desktop-template sandbox with gui_snapshot_interval > 0 (default). Path (a) needs a GUI click/type/key to be gated by policy or by the snapshot quota so a pending approval exists. Path (b) works under the default policy, which allows GUI tools.

Path (a): a human takes over the desktop and approves, or is approved on their behalf from the UI, a pending GUI approval while the lease is held. Path (b): a human takeover starts inside the agent's docker commit.

Path (b) needs the takeover to land inside the pre-input docker commit window. Path (a) is deterministic. The human must also start a non-windowed or new-session desktop-user process after the baseline, such as a terminal shell or a setsid/nohup job, before the burst closes.

execution.attacker_perspective: Prompt-injected agent holding the sandbox's agent token. It places or waits for a GUI click/type/key, which is sent so that it ends up as a pending approval or its docker commit overlaps a takeover, and later makes any tool call or GET /approvals/{aid} to trigger close_idle.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/click {"args":{"x":1,"y":1}} with a policy rule {id: gui-approval, tool: click, action: require_approval}
POST /approvals/{aid} {"decision":"approve"} by the human during the lease
GET /approvals/{aid} with the agent token after the idle window
docker exec -u desktop <container> setsid -f sleep 600 (stand-in for a human-opened terminal job)
instructions: Create a desktop sandbox with a policy rule gating click behind approval.
Agent sends click and receives 202 with an approval_id.
Human approves during the lease. The approval ends status failed (HumanControl) after a snapshot row is logged, and the burst stays open with a baseline taken during the lease.
Human starts a job in a new session, for example setsid sleep 600 as the desktop user or a terminal opened through noVNC.

After the idle window, the agent calls any tool or GET /approvals/{aid}. While the lease is still held, the audit log gets gui_processes_stopped (reason idle) listing the human's pid, and the process is gone.
